sections.headline: Wire crates were made for kennels, not *living rooms*
body: Your dog needs a spot of their own. Your living room doesn't need a metal cage in the corner.
So the crate gets a blanket thrown over it, or it ends up in a spare room, away from where you spend your time.

points.title: It's the first thing guests see
points.text: However you arrange the room, a wire crate still looks like a wire crate.

points.title: Covers never stay put
points.text: Blankets slide off, get pulled inside, and end up in the wash every week.

points.title: It takes a corner and gives nothing back
points.text: No surface, no storage. Just floor space you can't use.

sections.headline: The Den Table vs. a wire crate
rows: Holds a lamp, plant or books
None, unless you add a cover
sections.note: To be fair to wire crates: they fold flat for travel and cost less. If your dog is a heavy chewer or you travel with the crate, a wire crate may suit you better.

sections.headline: Find the right size
sections.lede: Your dog should be able to stand up, turn around and lie down comfortably inside.
steps: *Length:* with your dog standing, measure from the nose to the base of the tail. Add 2 to 4 inches.
*Height:* measure from the floor to the top of the head, or the ear tips if they stand up. Add 2 to 4 inches.
*Pick* the size whose inside measurements beat both numbers. Between sizes? Go up.
sections.note: Puppy still growing? Size for their adult weight. Not sure? Email us your dog's measurements and we'll help you choose.

a: It ships from a US warehouse, and most orders arrive 4 to 9 days after you order. You'll get a tracking link by email.
Use the size guide: measure your dog standing, add 2 to 4 inches, and pick the size with room to spare. If you're unsure, email us your dog's measurements and we'll help.

No crate is completely chew-proof, and this one is built to look like furniture. If your dog is a heavy chewer or still learning to settle in a crate, supervise them at first, or start with a wire crate.
